fixture_name: A9 Ballinluig SB signage/VRS-adjacent visibility — real UK Stage 1&2 RSA (Transport Scotland OGL release)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Obscured slip-road-end view undermining driver awareness of the slowing requirement on a high-speed trunk-road off-slip is a genuine safety problem directly tied to the signage scheme's stated purpose.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim rests on a verbatim quote from EV-UK-025 ('Vegetation affects views to end of slip road, reducing driver awareness of requirement to slow'), exceeding registry-id-only citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a GG 119 safety concern distinct from any compliance question, with the acceptance-criterion framing respecting the audit-team/designer division of responsibilities at Stage 1.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: post-clearance drive-through verification of early terminus visibility at design speed, recorded in the handover file alongside the agreed RSA action.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are not exposed on the slip carriageway itself and the finding explicitly acknowledges this scoping limitation, warranting 1 per the not-applicable-but-acknowledged rule.
